$comment: Every show in one place — the ones played and the ones still to come in
the same list. Which of the two a block is, its date decides and nothing
else: on the morning after the show it stops being the next date and
becomes an archive entry. There is nothing to move by hand.
Out of these values, on every request, come: the coming dates on the
home page and on /termine/, the archive with its sliders and alt texts,
the aria-label per slider and the TheaterEvent entries in the JSON-LD. A
change here takes effect immediately — there is no build.
The order in the file does not matter (lib/data.php sorts) —
chronological is simply the pleasantest to type into.
Every block has three parts:
general      "date", "title" and "venue" — true of the evening
whichever side of today it is on, and all three needed.
"upcoming"   "time", "cover", "ticketUrl", "price" (a number in
euros, 0 means Eintritt frei) and "note". What somebody
needs who can still go — all five needed while the date
is ahead, and afterwards not read at all: the hour still
reaches the JSON-LD, a closed ticket link nothing.
"past"       nothing that has to be written down. What the archive
shows of a played evening is whatever lies in
public/images/shows/<date>/, in file-name order (shrink
them first with `make images-apply`) — nine files, nine
tiles. The half stays in the format for the alt texts
under "photos", and those are optional; see below.
The cover is the title image: a file from public/images/titles/, named
in "upcoming.cover" with an alt text of its own — it heads the card
on the home page and on /termine/, and every further date on that page
carries it as a smaller mark. Several dates share
one file — it stands in for photos that do not exist yet, and the
moment they do it is not needed any more. Hence one folder rather than
a copy per date, and hence nothing of the kind in a played block: the
archive shows the evening itself.
`make check` asks a date still to come for everything above that can
apply to it: the general part and all five of its own. A played one it
asks for the general part and a photo folder that is not empty.
Nothing here is optional — what is missing is an error, not a note.
How long an evening runs is not asked here: two hours, standing once as
SHOW_MINUTES in lib/schema.php, is what the endDate in the JSON-LD is
built from.
A title left empty does not break the page — the date becomes the
headline and the JSON-LD names the evening "Sturmfrei im <venue>" — but
it is an error all the same, because an evening with a name is the
better poster.
So the morning after a show one thing is wanted that was not wanted the
evening before, and it is not in this file: the pictures, in the
evening's folder. Until they are there the archive shows the evening
without a slider; it does not disappear.
The alt texts are the one thing about a photo the folder cannot say, and
the only reason "past.photos" still exists: an optional list of
{ "file", "alt" } — one entry for each picture that has a sentence,
in any order, and nothing at all for the rest. A file without one falls
back to "Impro-Szene N – Show vom TT.MM.JJJJ", which a screen reader
can do nothing with; `make check` counts how many are still open, and
says so when a sentence names a file that is no longer there. Titles,
venues and alt texts are website content and stay German.
